# generator-shortcuts

**Question:** For this generator, name the strongest plausible shortcut or rival
rule that fits the canonical demonstrations. Give an exact input on which it
disagrees with the intended rule, how you checked the output, and whether your
proposed generator emits such cases.

## Economical rival: swap only the outer columns of each tile

The most economical plausible rival I tested is `swap_outer_columns_only`:
exchange the first and last columns inside each tile, leaving every interior
column untouched. For every width-three tile, this is exactly horizontal
reflection, regardless of its marks. Consequently it fits all three usable
canonical labeled pairs, not merely selected examples. I do not claim a ranking
among all conceivable rival programs.

## Exact emitted counterexample

Generated by v3.0.2, seed **314159**, sample index **1**,
difficulty **medium**, no overrides. It passes `self_check` and is
an ordinary default witness draw, not a hand-made unsupported grid.

Input, each digit one cell (5 rows by 23 columns):

```text
00330933000930000930303
03030933000903330930033
99999999999999999999999
03000930300900030903003
30330933000933330900003
```

Intended output from the unchanged Racket authority:

```text
03300900033900003930303
03030900033903330933003
99999999999999999999999
00030900303903000930030
03303900033903333930000
```

Outer-column-only rival output:

```text
00330903003900003930303
03030903003903330930033
99999999999999999999999
03000900303900030933000
00333903003903333930000
```

The first tile's top row is `00330`: reflection gives `03300`, but exchanging
only its two zero-valued outer cells leaves `00330`. Thus the witness specifically
teaches movement of the interior columns. It also refutes the other four declared
canonical-fitting rivals in the retained full counterexample.

## Verification and generator coverage

`checks/reference-probe/shortcut-counterexample.json` holds literal grids, both
outputs, generator/rule hashes and the source result index. The public command
was run from the packet root:

```sh
python3 run_with_racket.py python3 -m arcpuzzles apply ba29d14676d1 \
  --input ../checks/reference-probe/inputs.json \
  --out ../checks/reference-probe/racket.json
```

The case is result index 36 of 64. `checks/verify_authorities.py` compares every
returned Racket grid to an independent row-run oracle and asserts all five
canonical-fitting rivals disagree on this case. All **64/64** match. Rule hash
`93b766a34b8e`; final generator SHA-256 `a10720b648bf8a9d7b5bbe6c076b17b94119bc5c79869f4ec566ddfa89aef84e`.

Yes, the final generator emits such examples in its default witness profile.
Width 4–5 and an asymmetric interior pair are guaranteed there; another tile
row/column and non-4 color expose independent shortcuts. Two witnesses occur
in every six consecutive default draws, so five demos still contain one after
any one query holdout. Exact override choices can remove this teaching guarantee;
that limitation is explicit rather than hidden. The 300-lesson census and cyclic
window tests provide finite evidence against the declared rivals, not a proof
of identifiability against every possible rule.
